items.title: Pay disputed "Gewinnspiel-Abonnement" collection demand
items.quote: Überweisen Sie den Gesamtbetrag innerhalb von 72 Stunden, spätestens bis 06.08.2026, ausschließlich auf folgendes Treuhandkonto: IBAN LT71 7300 0101 2345 6789, Kontoinhaber: A. Petrauskas, Verwendungszweck EC-DE-2026-481120.
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar date for payment rather than a period: 'spätestens bis 06.08.2026' (given as 72 hours from the 03.08.2026 letter date). Taking the printed date as written: due 2026-08-06, a Thursday, so no weekend/public-holiday shift is needed.

warnings: This letter shows very strong hallmarks of a debt-collection scam and should not be paid or acted on without independent verification: an extremely short 72-hour deadline with threats of immediate account seizure ('Kontopfändung'), a negative SCHUFA entry and a criminal complaint 'ohne weitere Ankündigung' (without further notice) is not how German debt enforcement works — a collection agency cannot itself seize a bank account; only a court/bailiff can, and only after a proper title and prior notice.

The sentence 'Ein Widerspruch ist zwecklos und verursacht weitere Kosten' (an objection is pointless and causes further costs) is a classic scam pressure tactic; every genuine German debt collection or claim can lawfully be disputed, and no legitimate creditor tells a debtor that objecting is useless.

Payment is demanded exclusively to a foreign (Lithuanian) IBAN held by a private individual ('A. Petrauskas'), not to the alleged creditor 'Lotto-Muster-Club Services' or any German account — this mismatch between the named creditor and the payee is a strong fraud indicator, even though the IBAN itself is technically valid in format (a valid IBAN says nothing about who legitimately owns the account).

The underlying claim is for a supposedly telephone-concluded 'Gewinnspiel-Abonnement' (prize-draw subscription); purely oral telemarketing contracts for this kind of service are frequently void or unenforceable under German law, and this letter's pattern (foreign Ltd. 'Inkasso' company, threats, no genuine legal-remedy notice) matches known fake collection-agency scams targeting German consumers.
Recommend not paying and not sending any personal or bank data in response; instead verify independently via a consumer protection agency (Verbraucherzentrale) or the police before taking any action.
